newsitem.title: UK: IFC emerging market index up 0.7 pct at 288.02.
newsitem.headline: IFC emerging market index up 0.7 pct at 288.02.

text.p: The International Finance Corporation's composite index of emerging market equities, denominated in dollars, rose 0.7 percent to 288.02 at midsession on Thursday.
Latin America edged up 1.1 percent day-on-day to 525.16, Asia was up 0.1 percent at 247.49, and Europe, Middle East and Africa were up 1.6 percent at 130.29.
The IFC composite index touched a 1996 high of 308.77 on July 4, up from the year's 275.79 low, recorded on January 1.
ING Barings' Global Emerging Market Index, also denominated in dollars, was up 0.65 percent day-on-day at 156.97 at 1230 GMT.
The year's high was 165.948, reached on July 3. It touched the year's 148.85 low on January 2.
Morgan Stanley's dollar-denominated Emerging Markets Free index was up 0.62 percent at 466.280.
It touched a 1996 high of 505.452 on July 4. The year's 458.369 low was recorded on January 1.

All indices are capitalisation-weighted and are calculated daily. The IFC index measures returns on equities, liquid and accessible to foreign investors, from 26 emerging market countries. It is updated at 2300 GMT.
The BEMI index measures equity returns from some 20 emerging market countries, with the latest changes reported by 0900 GMT.
The MSCI Free measures equity returns from 22 emerging market nations. Changes are reported by 1300 GMT.
The J.P. Morgan emerging market bond index, its returns calculated in dollar terms, rose 0.17 percent to 124.17 by the start of trade on Thursday.
By region, Latin America was up 0.41 percent at 101.54, Asia rose 0.01 to 131.00 and East Europe was down 0.09 at 162.42.
